section_summary: This section contains diplomatic and political reporting from the American Embassy in Tokyo and the State Department's Division of Far Eastern Affairs covering August through October 1939. It focuses on the international fallout from the German-Soviet Non-Aggression Pact, the collapse of the Hiranuma Cabinet, and the installation of the Abe Cabinet, which proclaimed Japanese non-involvement in the European conflict while seeking an autonomous resolution to the China conflict. The documents detail major military and diplomatic developments including the Nomonhan border battle and truce with the Soviet Union, the offensive toward Changsha, escalating diplomatic friction with Great Britain and the United States over third-power rights in China, and sweeping state mobilization to impose price controls and economic reorganization.

subfiles.about: A comprehensive monthly report and lists of sent diplomatic communications reviewing Japanese political, diplomatic, military, and economic developments during August 1939.
subfiles.summary: Covers the political crisis triggered in Japan by the German-Soviet Non-Aggression Pact, which shattered deliberations for a military alliance with Germany and Italy and caused the resignation of Prime Minister Kiichiro Hiranuma and his Cabinet. Details the investiture of General Nobuyuki Abe's Cabinet, which adopted a free and independent foreign policy centered on concluding the China affair and strengthening the domestic wartime economy. Reports on heavy fighting at Nomonhan on the Outer Mongolian border, stalled military operations in China, the promotion of Wang Ching-wei's peace movement, and Anglo-Japanese tensions over anti-British demonstrations and customs disputes in China. Reviews economic strains including rising commodity prices, a 100 to 500 percent surge in commercial shipbuilding costs, bond flotations, and extensive regulations under the National Mobilization and Rice Distribution Control laws, followed by complete lists of despatches and telegrams sent to the State Department in August 1939.
subfiles.title: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of August 1939

subfiles.about: A State Department Far Eastern Affairs memorandum analyzing the Tokyo Embassy's August 1939 monthly report.
subfiles.from: Laurence E. Salisbury, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: States that Tokyo's monthly report for August 1939 competently summarizes principal events but provides little new information to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs, as key developments were previously reported. Highlights the finance and economic section for Mr. Jones, specifically noting data on escalating Japanese production costs showing that commercial shipbuilding costs per ton had risen 100 percent in a single year and 500 percent since July 1937.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo's Monthly Report for August 1939
subfiles.to: James M. Jones, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: A diplomatic despatch transmitting Report No. 156, a comprehensive survey of Japanese foreign relations, military operations, domestic politics, and economic conditions during September 1939.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits Report No. 156 detailing Japan's policy of non-involvement in the European war and its diplomatic request advising belligerent European nations to withdraw military forces and warships from occupied China. Records extensive American protests over the Japanese occupation of the Swatow Maritime Customs, illegal searches of American consular officials at Chefoo, interference with trade on the Yangtze, and the upcoming expiration of the 1911 commercial treaty. Describes the major Japanese military drive toward Changsha in northern Hunan, the unification of army commands under General Nishio and Lieutenant General Itagaki, the emergence of Wang Ching-wei as the prospective head of a new Chinese government, and the conclusion on September 16 of a border truce with the Soviet Union halting the Nomonhan conflict. Details domestic political actions including the appointment of Admiral Kichisaburo Nomura as Foreign Minister, sweeping wartime economic decrees freezing commodity prices, rents, and wages under the National Mobilization Law, and the formal pegging of the Japanese yen to the U.S. dollar, concluding with complete lists of despatches and telegrams sent during September 1939.
subfiles.title: Despatch Transmitting Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of September 1939 (Report No. 156)
subfiles.to: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State, Washington

subfiles.about: A State Department Far Eastern Affairs memorandum summarizing key points from the Tokyo Embassy's October 1939 monthly report.
subfiles.from: Cabot Coville, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Reviews Tokyo's despatch No. 4269 forwarding the October 1939 monthly report, highlighting statements by the Japanese Vice Governor of the Hua Hsin Commercial Bank on the planned elimination of the Chinese national currency under the projected puppet regime. Summarizes discussions at an economic conference in Tokyo regarding the self-sufficiency of the yen-bloc industrial structure, noting critical dependencies on foreign petroleum, copper, and rubber. Notes the shocking official admission by the Japanese War Office of 18,000 casualties at Nomonhan, the formalization of diplomatic ties with Germany and Italy through the replacement of Ambassadors Oshima and Shiratori, sluggish assimilation rates for national bonds (only 47.9 percent in October), and the official confirmation of the yen being pegged to the U.S. dollar at 23-7/16 cents.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 4269 (Report of Conditions in Japan for October 1939)
subfiles.to: Department of State / Division of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: A diplomatic despatch transmitting Report No. 157 on conditions in Japan during October 1939, accompanied by its table of contents and summary.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits the monthly report on conditions in Japan for October 1939 (Report No. 157) pursuant to standing Department instructions. Includes the report's detailed table of contents and index outlining major subjects: Ambassador Grew's address before the America-Japan Society, jurisdictional disputes in the Extra Settlement Roads Area of Shanghai and Kulangsu, consular searches at Chefoo, and Japanese-American relations. Outlines further sections covering British representations, military operations in China, the Japan-Manchukuo-China economic bloc, Soviet-Japanese relations following Nomonhan, German and Middle Eastern relations, and internal political friction within the Abe Cabinet over a proposed Trade Ministry.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4269 Transmitting Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of October 1939 (Report No. 157)
subfiles.to: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State, Washington
